sections.title: What You'll Learn
sections.content:
Ever wondered how your favorite apps are made? Software development isn't just coding - it's a step-by-step journey!

• The 7 key stages of building software
• How to turn ideas into working programs
• Why going back to fix things is totally normal

sections.title: Core Concepts
sections.content:
Imagine building a treehouse. You wouldn't just start hammering wood together! First you'd:

• Ask your friends what features they want (a slide? a trapdoor?)
• Sketch a blueprint
• Gather materials
• Build it piece by piece
• Test if it's safe
• Let everyone use it
• Fix any wobbly parts later

Software development works the same way! Here's how it breaks down:

• **Requirements**: Like asking your friends what they want in the treehouse. What should the software do?
• **Analysis**: Figuring out what materials (data) you need. What goes in? What comes out?
• **Design**: Drawing the blueprint. How will all the pieces fit together?

Each stage builds on the last, but sometimes you need to go back and fix things - just like realizing you need stronger wood after testing the treehouse!

sections.title: Code Examples
Key Points
points: Requirements specification defines what the program should accomplish
System analysis identifies the inputs, outputs, and processing needed
System design plans the program structure using pseudocode or flowcharts
Implementation translates the design into actual Java source code
Testing verifies the program works correctly using various test cases

sections.title: Summary
sections.content: Software development is a step-by-step process - not just coding. Always start with requirements - know what you're building. Break problems into small pieces (IPO: Input → Process → Output) Test early and often - catch bugs before users do.
